classification.difficultyReason: Follow the supplied intermediate expressions across linked right triangles; the hardest part requires subtracting a base segment before forming a new ratio for the angle.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $AC=7\tan50^{\circ}$ and $BC=7\tan25^{\circ}$, and hence find the length $AB$, correct to 1 mm.

spec.description: Two right triangles share DC. A, B and C lie on the same vertical line; the two adjacent angles at D are each 25 degrees.
spec.mathematics: DC=7 cm; angle BDC=25 degrees; angle ADB=25 degrees; angle DCA=90 degrees; B lies between A and C.

answer.worked:
In $\triangle ADC$, $\angle ADC=25^{\circ}+25^{\circ}=50^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan50^{\circ}&=\frac{AC}{7}\\AC&=7\tan50^{\circ}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
In $\triangle BDC$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan25^{\circ}&=\frac{BC}{7}\\BC&=7\tan25^{\circ}\text{ cm}\\AB&=AC-BC\\AB&=7(\tan50^{\circ}-\tan25^{\circ})\text{ cm}\\AB&=70(\tan50^{\circ}-\tan25^{\circ})\text{ mm}\\AB&\approx51\text{ mm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that $AP=20\sin56^{\circ}$, and hence find the length of $PC$, giving your answer correct to 1 cm.

spec.description: Triangle ABC is divided by perpendicular AP, with P between B and C.
spec.mathematics: AB=20 cm; angle ABC=56 degrees; angle ACB=46 degrees; AP is perpendicular to BC.

answer.worked:
In $\triangle ABP$:
$$\begin{align*}\sin56^{\circ}&=\frac{AP}{20}\\AP&=20\sin56^{\circ}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
In $\triangle APC$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan46^{\circ}&=\frac{AP}{PC}\\PC\tan46^{\circ}&=AP\\PC&=\frac{20\sin56^{\circ}}{\tan46^{\circ}}\\PC&\approx16\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that $PR=18\cos40^{\circ}$, find an expression for $PQ$, and hence find the angle $\alpha$, correct to the nearest minute.

spec.description: Right triangle PQR contains QS. S lies between P and R; alpha marks the acute interior angle PSQ.
spec.mathematics: QR=18 cm; SR=8 cm; angle PRQ=40 degrees; angle QPR=90 degrees; alpha=angle PSQ.

answer.worked:
In $\triangle PQR$:
$$\begin{align*}\cos40^{\circ}&=\frac{PR}{18}\\PR&=18\cos40^{\circ}\text{ cm}\\\sin40^{\circ}&=\frac{PQ}{18}\\PQ&=18\sin40^{\circ}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Since $SR=8$ cm:
$$\begin{align*}PS&=PR-SR\\PS&=18\cos40^{\circ}-8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
In $\triangle PSQ$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\alpha&=\frac{PQ}{PS}\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{18\sin40^{\circ}}{18\cos40^{\circ}-8}\\\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{18\sin40^{\circ}}{18\cos40^{\circ}-8}\right)\\\alpha&\approx63^{\circ}25'\end{align*}$$
